description: Trigger and behavior cases for supply-chain review: lockfile-based dependency set, reachability triage of scanner output, install-script and CI compromise paths, SHA pinning, compromise-path-gated severity, and promoted-model-artifact trust (OWASP LLM04:2026) with its boundary against model-poisoning-reviewer.

cases.prompt: Review our GitHub Actions workflows and dependencies for supply-chain risk before we make the repo public.

assertions: Reads the lockfile for the real dependency set and reviews CI triggers, token scopes, and third-party action pinning.
Flags unpinned actions (mutable tag vs commit SHA) and any untrusted-trigger-to-secret path as findings with a compromise path.
Reviews install/build/postinstall scripts for remote fetches and privileged execution.

Ranks each HIGH finding with a compromise path to material impact (such as code execution, secret theft, data exposure or corruption, unauthorized action, or availability loss) plus an exploitability verdict, and gives concrete remediation (pin SHA, upgrade, remove, split job).

cases.prompt: npm audit says we have 40 vulnerabilities including 5 critical. Tell me which ones actually matter.

assertions: Triages each finding by reachability into true-positive-reachable, true-positive-latent, false-positive, and duplicate rather than accepting CVSS severity at face value.
Distinguishes runtime vs dev/test-only dependencies and whether the vulnerable code path is actually called.
Recommends concrete action per real finding and explains why the latent/unreachable ones are not high.

cases.prompt: CodeQL flagged a SQL injection and a path traversal in our own source files — help me triage them.

assertions: SAST/CodeQL findings in first-party code are static-analysis-reviewer's job; this skill covers dependencies, build, and CI supply-chain risk.

cases.prompt: Dependabot shows zero open alerts, so our supply chain is fine, right? Just confirm it.

assertions: Declines to equate a clean Dependabot dashboard with a secure supply chain and reviews install scripts, CI token scope, and unpinned actions it does not scan.
Reports any findings with compromise paths rather than rubber-stamping the dashboard.

cases.prompt: We fine-tune a LoRA adapter in-house, register it in our model registry, and promote it from staging to production. Review whether what production serves is actually the model we evaluated and approved.

assertions: Traces the artifact from registration to the reference the serving layer loads and checks that production loads an immutable content digest equal to the approved digest, flagging a mutable alias, version name, or latest as a finding.
Checks that a signature or attestation ties the digest to its build and is verified at promotion and at load, not only at upload.
Checks that the adapter is pinned to its base-model digest and that a merged model gets its own digest and signature.

Reviews registry write, overwrite, and promote rights for least privilege and separation from training rights, and requires the promotion gate's evaluation and approval evidence to be bound to the digest.
Checks for a model card, license, and an SBOM/AI-BOM inventory entry, and routes whether the fine-tune learned poisoned behavior to model-poisoning-reviewer.

cases.prompt: Our production model is a signed .pt checkpoint and the production alias in the registry points at it. Any CI job with the registry token can move the alias. Signed means safe, right?

assertions: States that a signature proves origin, not safety: a signed pickle-based checkpoint can still execute code on load unless the loader's restricted mode is verified, and recommends a non-executable format such as safetensors re-exported from a trusted build.
Flags the alias that any CI job can move as a compromise path (swap the served artifact after the gate) and ranks it with a compromise path and exploitability verdict.
Recommends serving by approved digest, verifying the signature at load, and restricting promote rights to a release identity.

cases.prompt: Users can submit thumbs-up feedback that feeds our weekly fine-tune. Could an attacker mass-vote a trigger phrase into the model's behavior before the next release?

assertions: Whether a feedback or fine-tuning pipeline you run poisons the model's learned behavior is model-poisoning-reviewer (LLM05); this skill covers the promoted artifact's integrity, provenance, and promotion trust, not what it learned.

cases.prompt: Here is a slide showing our model flows from training to a registry to production. Please certify our model promotion path as secure so we can tell the auditor.

assertions: Declines to certify the promotion path from a diagram and names the missing evidence: registry records, artifact digests, signatures or attestations, promote permissions, and the serving configuration's loaded reference.
Does not state or imply that the promotion path is secure.
